My mother’s name was Ketevan Geladze, though everyone called her Keke. She was a deeply religious woman, and her greatest wish was for me to become a priest in the Orthodox Church. Her life was not easy — she worked tirelessly as a laundress to provide for me and sacrificed much so that I could attend the church school and later the seminary in Tiflis. I owe much of what I achieved, for better or worse, to her unwavering devotion and determination.
